impact.affected_asset: Availability of the PHP application or worker performing YAML parsing.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause a PHP process using the Symfony YAML parser to crash by supplying deeply nested YAML, where the application accepts arbitrary YAML input.
impact.security_effect: Denial of service through a crashed PHP parser worker/process.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker able to submit arbitrary YAML provides a document with deeply nested block structures.
Nested-block parsing did not impose a maximum recursion depth; the advisory further describes missing depth limiting across block-level and inline parsing.

On an indented line, Parser::doParse() calls parseBlock(); parseBlock() instantiates a parser and calls doParse() for the indented content, repeating the mutual-recursion cycle for each nesting level until PHP stack/resources are exhausted.
PHP raises a fatal error and the worker/process parsing the document crashes, causing denial of service.

failure.operation: Unbounded doParse()/parseBlock() mutual recursion exhausts the PHP stack/resources and yields a fatal error.

primary_invariant.statement: Recursive YAML parsing of untrusted nested structures must be bounded by a maximum nesting depth shared across parser paths.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The reported block parser's doParse()/parseBlock() mutual recursion had no maximum content-depth limit, allowing each indentation level to introduce another recursive parsing operation.

quality.review_notes: The audit supplies a finding-level block-parser mechanism and a PHP harness invocation using an attached test_recursion.yaml, but the bundle does not contain that YAML attachment or captured execution/stack-trace output. The repository artifact is only a rendered project page, not the cited patch/test diff. Consequently, no executed result or regression-test coverage is asserted; advisory language about inline parsing is retained as complementary scope rather than attributed to the audit's block-level trace.

remediation.invariant_restored: Parser recursion is tracked in a shared ParserState and constrained by a default maximum nesting depth of 128 across block-level and inline parsing; callers may configure the limit through Parser::__construct(), Yaml::parse(), and Yaml::parseFile().
mitigation_classes: shared recursion-depth state across parsing paths

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The application must pass attacker-controlled YAML to the parser.
data_structure_invariants: Nested YAML parse transitions must have a finite maximum depth.
Depth accounting must cover recursive parser paths that process the same input document.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The patched default is 128 according to the advisory; the vulnerable condition requires nesting sufficiently deep to exhaust PHP stack/resources.
numeric_domains.name: maximum nesting depth

state_context.state_machine: For each indented YAML block, doParse() delegates to parseBlock(), which creates a parser and invokes doParse() on the indented content; without a nesting bound, this transition repeats for deeper blocks.
